fullPassage:
Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. This gas itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in everyday situations. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change.

While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting solutions available. In this report, we will focus on one of the most powerful nature-based solutions to climate change: whales, the giant helpers living under the sea.

Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons, and some whales have been known to live for more than 100 years. These giants do extremely beneficial things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death. According to scientists, a single whale can absorb about 550 kilograms of CO2 per year, while a tree can absorb only 22.

Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This achievement is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then store it underground.

In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help circulate nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean.

These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through photosynthesis, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees. Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the ocean's bottom, their movements stir up the water and bring nutrients down to the creatures living below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine life at various depths throughout the ocean.

Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year. For example, in the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii.

Nutrients are relatively scarce in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, encourage the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased carbon absorption throughout the entire ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to combat climate change.

Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. The number of whales had dramatically dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially banned in 1986. It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean. It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to address this global challenge. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a (A)[significant / negligible] amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. However, (B)[excessive / minimal] amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously (C)[threatening / protecting] life on our planet. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We must act immediately to stop any further climate change. While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인간 활동은 상당한(significant) CO2를 발생시켰고, 과도한(excessive) 양이 온실효과에 기여했으며, 지구 생명체를 심각하게 위협하고(threatening) 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① significant — excessive — threatening: 원문 일치
❌ ② negligible(무시할 수 있는): significant의 반의어
❌ ③ minimal(최소한의): excessive의 반의어
❌ ④ protecting(보호하는): threatening의 반의어
det.tip: significant(상당한) ↔ negligible(무시할 수 있는), excessive(과도한) ↔ minimal(최소한의), threatening(위협하는) ↔ protecting(보호하는)

questions.passage: While many high-tech solutions such as carbon capture have been proposed, they are often too expensive to be used widely. Fortunately, there are also low-tech, (A)[economical / costly], and even long-lasting solutions available. Whales are amazing creatures. They are (B)[enormous / tiny] and live incredibly long lives. These giants do extremely (C)[beneficial / harmful] things for the environment throughout their long lives and even after death.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 경제적이고(economical), 거대하며(enormous), 환경에 매우 유익한(beneficial) 일을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② economical — enormous — beneficial: 원문 일치
❌ ① tiny(작은): enormous의 반의어
❌ ③ costly(비싼): economical의 반의어
❌ ④ harmful(해로운): beneficial의 반의어
det.tip: economical(경제적인) ↔ costly(비싼), enormous(거대한) ↔ tiny(작은), beneficial(유익한) ↔ harmful(해로운)

questions.passage: Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean. These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and (A)[insignificant / essential], but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is (B)[equivalent / unrelated] to planting 2 billion new trees. Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious risk. It is important to recognize that protecting them is an effective and (C)[cost-efficient / wasteful] way to address this global challenge. Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the ocean.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 작고 하찮아(insignificant) 보이지만, 1% 증가는 나무 20억 그루와 맞먹고(equivalent), 고래 보호는 비용 효율적(cost-efficient)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ insignificant — equivalent — cost-efficient: 원문 일치
❌ ① unrelated(무관한): equivalent의 반의어
❌ ② essential(필수적인): insignificant의 반의어. 'may look' 뒤에 부정적 인상이 와야 but으로 전환
❌ ④ wasteful(낭비적인): cost-efficient의 반의어
det.tip: insignificant(하찮은) ↔ essential(필수적인). may look insignificant but play a significant role → 양보+역접 구조.

questions.passage: Whales are amazing creatures. They are ①<u>enormous</u> and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons. According to scientists, a single whale can ②<u>absorb</u> about 550 kilograms of CO2 per year, while a tree can absorb only 22. Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and ③<u>habitats</u> for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a whale fall. Whale falls ④<u>temporarily</u> bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '영구적으로(permanently)'인데 '일시적으로(temporarily)'로 바뀌었다. CO2를 영구적으로 매장한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① enormous(거대한): 원문 일치
✅ ② absorb(흡수하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ habitats(서식지): 원문 일치
❌ ④ temporarily(일시적으로) → permanently(영구적으로): 반의어 교체
det.tip: permanently(영구적으로) ↔ temporarily(일시적으로). 해저에 '영구적으로' 묻는다는 것이 탄소 포집의 핵심.

questions.passage: Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an ①<u>enormous</u> amount of waste. This waste is ②<u>rich</u> in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some ③<u>microscopic</u> creatures floating at the surface of the ocean. Nutrients are relatively ④<u>abundant</u> in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문은 '부족한(scarce)'인데 '풍부한(abundant)'으로 바뀌었다. 따뜻한 바다에는 영양분이 부족해서 플랑크톤 생존이 어렵다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ abundant(풍부한) → scarce(부족한): 반의어 교체. '어렵게 만든다(makes it difficult)'와 abundant는 모순
✅ ② rich(풍부한): 원문 일치
✅ ③ microscopic(미세한): 원문 일치
✅ ① enormous(엄청난): 원문 일치
det.tip: scarce(부족한) ↔ abundant(풍부한). '부족해서 생존이 어려운' 인과관계.

questions.passage: Despite the important roles of whales in our environment, their lives are at serious ①<u>risk</u>. The number of whales had ②<u>dramatically</u> dropped until killing them for commercial purposes was officially ③<u>banned</u> in 1986. Today, whales are still ④<u>protected</u> by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '위협받고 있는(threatened)'인데 '보호받고 있는(protected)'으로 바뀌었다. 어망, 선박 충돌 등으로 여전히 위협받고 있다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① risk(위험): 원문 일치
✅ ② dramatically(극적으로): 원문 일치
✅ ③ banned(금지된): 원문 일치
❌ ④ protected(보호받는) → threatened(위협받는): 반의어. '위험 요소들에 의해' 뒤에 protected는 모순
det.tip: threatened(위협받는) ↔ protected(보호받는). 어망, 선박 충돌, 미세플라스틱 = 위협 요소.

questions.passage: Over the past two centuries, human activities have generated a significant amount of carbon dioxide, commonly referred to as CO2. However, excessive amounts of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to the greenhouse effect, resulting in a gradual increase in the Earth's surface temperature. To make matters worse, this increase has sped up in recent years. We must act __________ to stop any further climate change.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 이상의 기후 변화를 막기 위해 즉각(immediately) 행동해야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ immediately(즉각): 원문 일치. 긴급한 행동 요구
❌ ① gradually(점차적으로): 즉각의 반대
❌ ② occasionally(가끔): 긴급성에 안 맞음
❌ ④ temporarily(일시적으로): 지속적 행동 필요
det.tip: immediately = at once = right away = 즉각, 당장.

questions.passage: In addition to their direct absorption and burial of CO2 through whale falls, whales also make a significant indirect contribution to reducing CO2 through an act called a whale pump. This refers to the vertical movements of whales that help __________ nutrients across different depths of the ocean. Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near the surface, they release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures living in that area.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고래의 수직 움직임은 바다의 여러 깊이에 걸쳐 영양분을 순환시키는(circulate) 데 도움을 준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② circulate(순환시키다): 원문 일치
❌ ① deplete(고갈시키다): 순환의 반대
❌ ③ contaminate(오염시키다): 부정적 의미
❌ ④ preserve(보존하다): 순환과 다른 의미
det.tip: circulate(순환시키다): 위아래로 영양분을 돌게 하다. whale pump = 영양분 순환 장치.

questions.passage: These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through __________, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is estimated that increasing the world's phytoplankton by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 탄소, 물, 빛을 사용하여 에너지를 만드는 과정인 광합성(photosynthesis)을 통해 이를 수행한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① photosynthesis(광합성): 원문 일치. carbon + water + light → energy
❌ ② decomposition(분해): 에너지 생성이 아닌 물질 분해
❌ ③ evaporation(증발): 물이 기체가 되는 과정
❌ ④ fermentation(발효): 미생물에 의한 분해
det.tip: photosynthesis = photo(빛) + synthesis(합성) = 광합성. 탄소+물+빛 → 에너지.

questions.passage: Whales are amazing creatures. They are <u>enormous</u> and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh over 200 tons.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>enormous</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 고래는 거대하다(enormous) = 거대한(huge).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ huge(거대한): enormous의 동의어
❌ ① tiny(작은): enormous의 반의어
❌ ② ordinary(평범한): 크기와 무관
❌ ③ elegant(우아한): 다른 의미
det.tip: enormous = huge = immense = massive = 거대한.

questions.passage: It is estimated that the global whale population fell from 4 to 5 million to just over 1 million during the decades before the ban. Today, whales are still threatened by various man-made dangers, such as fishing nets, ship strikes, and microplastic pollution in the ocean. It is important to recognize that whales are valuable partners in our fight against the climate crisis and that protecting them is an effective and cost-efficient way to <u>address</u> this global challenge. Let's take action to help more whales live longer and healthier lives.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>address</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 이 전 지구적 난관을 처리하다(address) = 해결하다(tackle).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ tackle(해결하다, 다루다): address의 동의어 (문제를 다루다)
❌ ① ignore(무시하다): address의 반의어
❌ ② create(만들다): 문제를 만드는 것은 반대
❌ ④ worsen(악화시키다): 반대 방향
det.tip: address a problem = tackle a problem = deal with a problem = 문제를 다루다/해결하다.

questions.passage: This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of many marine animals and, importantly, <u>encourage</u> the growth of phytoplankton even in warm waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to increased carbon absorption throughout the entire ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every corner of the ocean, helping to combat climate change.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>encourage</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 따뜻한 바다에서도 플랑크톤 성장을 촉진한다(encourage) = 촉진하다(promote).
det.analysis:
✅ ② promote(촉진하다): encourage의 동의어
❌ ① discourage(억제하다): encourage의 반의어
❌ ③ restrict(제한하다): 촉진의 반대
❌ ④ measure(측정하다): 다른 의미
det.tip: encourage = promote = foster = 촉진하다, 장려하다.

questions.passage: As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. Nutrients are relatively <u>scarce</u> in warm waters, which makes it difficult for phytoplankton to survive. Fortunately, when the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>scarce</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 영양분이 부족한(scarce) ↔ 풍부한(abundant).
det.analysis:
✅ ① abundant(풍부한): scarce의 반의어
❌ ② limited(제한된): scarce와 유사
❌ ③ rare(희귀한): scarce와 유사
❌ ④ insufficient(불충분한): scarce와 유사
det.tip: scarce(부족한) ↔ abundant(풍부한). 따뜻한 바다에 영양분이 부족하다.

questions.passage: Specifically, it creates the perfect growing conditions for some microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the ocean. These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look tiny and <u>insignificant</u>, but when taken together, they play a significant role in reducing CO2. They absorb about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce about 50% of the atmosphere's oxygen. They do this through photosynthesis, a process that creates energy using carbon, water, and light.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>insignificant</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 하찮은(insignificant) ↔ 결정적인(crucial).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ crucial(결정적인, 중요한): insignificant의 반의어
❌ ① trivial(사소한): insignificant와 유사
❌ ② minor(사소한): insignificant와 유사
❌ ③ negligible(무시할 만한): insignificant와 유사
det.tip: insignificant(하찮은) ↔ crucial/significant/important(중요한). in- 접두사 = 부정.

questions.passage:
(A) Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small fish. The word <u>feed</u> here means to eat.
(B) The farmer went to the barn to <u>feed</u> the animals before sunrise.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 feed가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) feed on = ~을 먹다(자동사). (B) feed the animals = 동물에게 먹이를 주다(타동사).
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 먹다 — (B) 먹이를 주다: feed on(먹다) vs feed(먹이를 주다)
❌ ① 의미 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 공급하다: feed on은 '먹다'
❌ ④ 공급하다: (B)는 동물에게 먹이를 주다
det.tip: feed on = ~을 먹다 (자동사). feed + 목적어 = ~에게 먹이를 주다 (타동사).

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"to move regularly between places at different times of the year, especially of birds or animals"

det.korean: 연중 특정 시기에 장소 사이를 정기적으로 이동하다 = 이동하다(migrate).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ migrate(이주하다): 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ① hibernate(동면하다): 이동이 아닌 잠자기
❌ ② reproduce(번식하다): 다른 의미
❌ ④ populate(거주하다): 이동이 아님
det.tip: migrate = 이주하다, 이동하다. migration(명사). 혹등고래가 알래스카↔하와이를 이동.

questions.passage: Whale falls permanently bury about 145,000 tons of CO2 under the sea every year. This __________ (achieve) is basically what expensive carbon capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon and then store it underground.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이러한 성과(achievement)는 비싼 탄소 포집 기술이 목표로 하는 것이다.
det.analysis: achieve(동사) → achievement(명사): 'This ___'에서 주어 역할이므로 명사 필요
det.tip: achieve(동사, 성취하다) → achievement(명사, 성과, 성취). -ment = 명사 접미사.

questions.passage: Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also __________ (horizon) through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant mammals migrate over long distances at certain times of the year.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 수직뿐 아니라 수평으로(horizontally)도 영양분을 퍼뜨린다.
det.analysis: horizon(명사) → horizontally(부사): 'not only vertically but also ___'에서 부사 병렬
det.tip: horizon(명사, 지평선) → horizontal(형용사, 수평의) → horizontally(부사, 수평으로). vertically(수직으로) ↔ horizontally(수평으로).

questions.passage: According to scientists, a single whale can absorb about 550 kilograms of CO2 per year, while a tree can absorb only 22. Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean floor with all the CO2 they absorbed during their lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats for deep-sea creatures. This process is called __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고래가 죽어 해저에 가라앉는 과정은 고래 낙하(a whale fall)라고 불린다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ a whale fall(고래 낙하): 원문 일치
❌ ① a whale pump: 수직 이동으로 영양분 순환하는 과정
❌ ② photosynthesis: 광합성
❌ ③ the greenhouse effect: 온실 효과
det.tip: whale fall = 고래 낙하: 죽은 고래가 해저에 가라앉아 CO2를 영구 매장하는 과정.

questions.passage: Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only vertically but also horizontally through a process called the great whale conveyor belt. In the summer, humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where the water is cold but rich in nutrients. As winter approaches, they travel up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters near Hawaii. When the whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich waste. This process can be thought of as __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: a method of protecting whales from commercial hunting
a conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters to warm waters
a way for whales to escape from predators in Alaska
a technology to capture carbon dioxide from the atmosphere

det.korean: 이 과정은 차가운 바다에서 따뜻한 바다로 영양분을 이동시키는 컨베이어 벨트로 여겨진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conveyor belt from cold to warm waters: 원문 일치
❌ ② 상업 포경 보호: 다른 맥락
❌ ③ 포식자 탈출: 해당 내용 없음
❌ ④ 대기 탄소 포집 기술: 인공 기술이지 자연 과정이 아님
det.tip: great whale conveyor belt = 거대한 고래 컨베이어 벨트: 알래스카(차가운 물) → 하와이(따뜻한 물)로 영양분을 운반.
